findings.span: the further it has travelled against that wall, the less it has
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: the sheet runs three / five / eleven with distance from the vessel, so the figure RISES as the warning weakens; eleven is the worst reading on the run, not a good one

findings.span: The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything.
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: the quarter-turns are how he opens the valve; the span defines the recorded figure as the dilution fraction, not a count of turns

findings.span: The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run, is the same bore, comes off the same vessel and the same fill, and reads three at both ends.
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: a longer line reads the same three as the nearest house, so the figures cannot be derived from pipe length; they are sniffed off the box

justification: Key C restates the definitional span word for word (share of gas in air at first smell). No option is left unaddressed. Key span: “The box counts in parts of gas to a thousand parts of air: the figure he writes down is the fraction he needs in front of him before he can smell anything.”

findings.span: What warns you at a cooker is ethyl mercaptan, a sulphur compound put into the gas at the depot at a fixed weight to a fixed volume.
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: dosing is at the depot, not at the estate after the joints are proved

findings.span: Bare oxide takes the most, so a main scrubs hardest in the week it goes into service
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: adsorption is greatest at the start and falls with age; the oxide is already there ('a bloom of rust from the weeks the lengths stood in the yard'), so the take does not begin once the steel corrodes in service. The sticking half of the option is true; the temporal clause is what kills it

findings.span: the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: explicitly denies that the odorant arrives more or less intact

justification: Key A maps clause for clause onto the span: 'partly' = Some, 'changed into another compound' = oxidised into a disulphide, 'the nose can hardly pick up' = it hardly smells. Key span: “Some is oxidised on contact into a disulphide, a serviceable molecule that is no use as a warning, because it hardly smells.”

findings.span: The old steel line that has fed the farm buildings since the sixties is longer than the new run
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: the passage states the opposite of 'short enough': it is LONGER than the run that fails

findings.span: is the same bore
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: bore is explicitly held equal, so a narrower bore cannot be the explanation

findings.span: comes off the same vessel and the same fill
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: same vessel and same fill, so not a supply of its own

justification: Key D is carried by the saturation rule plus 'reads three at both ends' and 'Age works the other way about.' The passage builds an explicit three-way control (length, bore, source) so that only age survives. Key span: “Once a stretch of wall has taken all it can hold it stops taking, and the gas goes past unchanged.”

findings.span: What he cannot do is put a date on the end of it in advance.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: doubly dead: the dose is 'three or four times the ordinary dose', and no end date can be fixed in advance

findings.span: one call-out to a kitchen where the cooker is off and the smell is only the soak costs more than the odorant does
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: explicitly denies that the odorant is the main cost

findings.span: you do it before the first burner is lit
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: explicitly places pickling before the houses are in use; the closing scene has the cooker still capped

justification: Key B restates the span: the end is determined by re-walking the run and reading it, not by a calendar. The closing figure of six against a working threshold of four confirms the soak is still open, which is consistent with the key. Key span: “The soak ends when the readings say it has ended, which means walking the run again.”

findings.span: The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: explicitly rules out a bad fill; the old line runs off the same fill and reads three

findings.span: the gas that leaves the far end has less smell in it than the gas that went in, and the further it has travelled against that wall, the less it has
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: the loss happens along the run, not at the outlet, so the warning does not survive the run

findings.span: The pipe that needs watching is the pipe nobody has ever used.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: the world-canonical belief (new plant is the safe plant) is stated and denied outright

justification: Key D is the synthesis the whole piece is built for: 'every joint was pressure-tested, the paperwork is signed' with a reading of eleven against a working threshold of four. Every component of the key is on a span. Key span: “The slope is not a fault in the pipe and it is not a fault in the fill.”

findings.span: There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: 'nothing modern about it either' is planted against a 'Nowadays' reading; the clause reports this household's eleven years, not a change in the era

findings.span: There is nothing unusual in that house, and nothing modern about it either. In almost any house, one person knows which way the boiler override goes, which radiator to bleed first, which bin week it is.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it

findings.span: The hall carpet took most of the damage.
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: the run of the paragraph is a tally of loss, so a 'fortunately' connective is the wrong polarity

justification: Key D ('Worse') is licensed by the evaluative relative clause 'which is long enough to have asked', which marks the eleven years as an aggravating fact rather than a neutral or mitigating one. Key span: “which is long enough to have asked”

findings.span: This competence is not earned and not handed out.

findings.span: It may sit with the owner, the owner’s daughter, or the man who rents the back bedroom.

findings.span: This competence is not earned and not handed out.

findings.span: The knowledge holds no office and is not bought with the house.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it

findings.span: somebody who was in the right room on the right morning and has answered questions ever since
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: acquisition is an accident of presence; nothing is chosen, and a cold is not chosen either

justification: Key B is carried by the in-sentence simile: a cold is caught. The verb is fixed by the comparison, not merely by elimination. Key span: “the way a cold is, by being in the room when it happens”

findings.span: no rule, no principle, nothing that carries to another house
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: an instance instantiates a general rule; the span denies that any rule or principle exists

findings.span: nobody disputes them
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: opinions are disputable; the span denies disputability

findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it
findings.note: an anecdote narrates; these items name and are four words long

Key span: “It names one thing in one building and explains nothing; most are four words long; nobody disputes them.”

findings.span: Ask, and you will be told gladly and at length, and still have nothing.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it

justification: Key C is supported by the immediately preceding sentence and by 'In almost any house, one person knows...'. It is the only filler under which the concessive 'Although X, it moves one way only' actually concedes: ordinary knowledge that nonetheless travels only by co-presence. Key span: “Nothing on that list is difficult and nothing on it is being kept back.”

findings.span: Before starting she played a dozen notes into her meter, the last of them from the top octave, and it drew her a curve for all eighty-eight notes from this piano’s own figure.

findings.span: so this upright’s figure is larger than a grand’s, its short thick strings already counted in it

findings.span: The extra cents are not an allowance for the cold: a winter takes the whole instrument down together, and that is another visit.

findings.span: The Shenwolds sit three miles off that road, up a lane the coaches did not use.
findings.category: refuted by a span asserting something incompatible with it

findings.span: Upper Shenwold has no market of its own.
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: the Thursday is shared because the two lie ten minutes' walk apart, not because both hold markets

findings.span: the Thursday market is the largest of the four
findings.category: refuted by a span that explicitly negates it
findings.note: the biggest crowd is Thursday's, not Nerresby's Tuesday

justification: Key A is four-for-four against the card: Monday/Haddenthorpe, Tuesday/Nerresby, Wednesday/Thrapmere ('Thrapmere fills on a Wednesday and Lower Shenwold on a Thursday'), Thursday/Shenwold. The mileages (9, then 30 back through Haddenthorpe, then 4 out again) make the order travel-inefficient, and the 1227 charter predates the 1769 turnpike by 542 years, so the days govern the road rather than the reverse. Key span: “Haddenthorpe has kept its Monday market since a charter of 1227, and Nerresby has held a Tuesday one for as long.”

findings.span: Storlekarna följer ingen jämn trappa.
